transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-31
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (Voyage CTO), Marco Reyes (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — figure out your p95 targets, what traffic looks like, discuss hosted/dedicated/private, and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Dana: yep, perfect. rough context — we power real-time personalization and a chat assistant inside our product. latency's a big deal for UX. we've had some spikes, and we think model overhead plus our seq lens cause trouble.
[00:35] Marco: to add, most requests are short — 20 to 80 tokens — but we have bursts where seq len goes to 512 for some long summarization. our SLA target customer-facing is p95 under 300ms for the short path, and for streaming chat p95 end-to-end under 1s to first token and steady token rate after.
[00:58] Priya (SE): okay great, so two distinct profiles — short synchronous completions and streaming. can you tell us concurrency at peak? tokens/sec?
[01:12] Marco: typical steady is ~200 concurrent users hitting the assistant, peaks to ~1,400 concurrent in bursts. token rate steady ~3k tokens/sec across the fleet, bursts up to 28k tokens/sec for 30 to 120 seconds.
[01:32] Alex: understood. and are you currently on-prem or cloud? which model infra?
[01:36] Sofia: everything in AWS—EKS with a mix of g4dn and g5 nodes. models run in-house using a homegrown inference layer, not optimized for KV cache and streaming so far.
[01:49] Dana: also curious about data residency — some of our customers require EU-only hosting, so private or VPC options are interesting.
[01:58] Priya: good — that'll affect routing and fallback. quick question: what's the exact p95 metric you use? end-to-end from client to first token or server processing?
[02:10] Marco: we track client-to-client but for vendor evals we usually ask for server-side p95 to first token, and tokens/sec for sustained throughput.
[02:20] Alex: perfect. so on Redwood side we measure server p95 to first token and end-to-end depending on telemetry; we can map to your metrics if you share the traces.
[02:34] [short cross-talk] Dana: okay show us options — hosted first? dedicated? private? what's the tradeoff?
[02:45] Alex: simple summary — Hosted is fastest to get started, low friction, usage-based; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable p95 and throughput with an SLA; Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency and full control. cost and latency predictability increase as you move toward dedicated/private.
[03:08] Priya: and from a runtime angle — streaming p95 is influenced heavily by batching, continuous KV cache warm state, and kernel selection. for short requests, small-batch optimizations and prefix caching push p95 down a lot.
[03:25] Marco: what's your experience on p95 with short requests on hosted? numbers?
[03:30] Priya: example ballpark — for a 50-token completion on a optimized model family we measure server p95 to first token ~120-220ms on hosted depending on region and load; with dedicated and pinned capacity that can go down further and be more consistent. streaming first token is similar if you avoid large batching delays.
[03:49] Dana: ping, how about burst behavior — we saw big drops when lots of concurrent short requests hit. do you do auto-fallback?
[03:57] Alex: yes, smart routing + fallbacks — Redwood can route to lower-capacity or quantized variants if primary model is saturated; automatic canary and fallback policy. for bursts you can do reserved burst pools or pre-warmed nodes.
[04:12] Marco: any magic for reducing token/sec cost without hurting p95?
[04:16] Priya: batching helps throughput, but there's tradeoff with latency. KV cache/prefix cache is very effective when you have repeated context — avoids recomputing earlier layers. also quantized model variants for background tasks; also consider caching the first N tokens for templated prompts.
[04:33] Marco: sounds promising. can Redwood run a benchmark against our traces?
[04:36] Alex: yes — if you share a 48–72 hour tokens/sec trace with seq len distribution we can run a replay and estimate p95/throughput on hosted and dedicated topologies. that's one of the next steps we mentioned.
[04:50] Dana: okay, expectation setting: we want a reproducible benchmark and then a pilot for canary. timeline — we'd like results in 2 weeks. is that realistic?
[04:59] Priya: 2 weeks is doable if we get the traces and test model selection. for private/on-prem it takes longer because of access and security review.
[05:10] [00:05:10 to 00:20:00 — mid-call detailed exchange]
[05:10] Priya: on dedicated sizing: with your peak 28k tokens/sec bursts and seq len percentiles, rough starting point might be a small cluster of A10/RTX-capable GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscale burst pool. exact numbers depend on model family and batch profile.
[05:28] Marco: we run a Llama-derived 13B and a smaller 7B for quick replies — how does that change sizing?
[05:35] Priya: 13B increases KV/cache footprint and per-token compute, so more GPU cycles. for streaming chat you'd want to serve 13B on dedicated nodes and use 7B as fast-fallback for non-critical completions. that approach keeps p95 stable.
[05:49] Sofia: how about security — SOC 2 and KMS requirements — we need audit logs and to manage keys.
[05:56] Alex: Redwood supports SOC 2 and common compliance artifacts; for Private we allow customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. Hosted supports envelope encryption and audit retention add-ons. we'll send the security pack.
[06:08] Marco: and SSO/SSO mapping? we have SAML SSO for internal tools — we need RBAC for team members.
[06:14] Alex: SAML/SSO and RBAC available — we'll include the integration guide.
[06:20] Dana: what about multi-region and EU-only routing?
[06:24] Priya: smart routing can pin requests to region and fallback to same-region compatible model variant; for strict data residency you'd choose Private (VPC) or Dedicated with region-specific pools.
[06:36] Marco: what telemetry do you provide? we need token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, traces.
[06:42] Alex: Redwood Console has token-level cost and per-route dashboards, traces, and rollout controls. we'll share a sample dashboard export.
[06:50] [light interruption] Guest voice: sorry, small question — if we do hosted first, how do we migrate to dedicated later without changing SDKs?
[06:57] Priya: same API surface — deployment and routing abstracted. you can pin model versions and rollout independently. minimal client changes.
[07:07] Marco: what's a typical SLA for dedicated?
[07:10] Alex: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets are part of reserved capacity contracts — we'll put numbers in the pricing doc.
[07:18] Dana: ok, let's discuss benchmarks — we want a third-party baseline vs your hosted and for dedicated. do you run both?
[07:25] Priya: yes, once we get traces we'll run an internal replay on hosted, and then spin a dedicated test cluster to compare. we can also run quantized variants to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:38] Marco: small nit — are synthetic loads representative? sometimes they hide head-of-line issues.
[07:44] Priya: we prefer replay of real traces; synthetic can show extremes but doesn't capture seq len skews or user think time.
[07:53] Alex: agreed. please include real client timestamps so we can map to end-to-end.
[08:00] [08:00 to 00:50:00 — remainder: wrapping technical clarifications and logistics]
[08:00] Marco: will Redwood share a recommended model + quantization profile?
[08:04] Priya: yes, we'll propose model families and quantization/hybrid configs based on your accuracy requirements.
[08:10] Sofia: any network recommendations? our users mostly hit EU region — we want to avoid cross-region latency.
[08:16] Priya: for EU focus, pin region, pre-warm KV caches in that region and ensure egress is minimized. for private we can deploy inside your VPC in the region.
[08:26] Dana: what's the typical docs you send after a call like this?
[08:29] Alex: pricing/TCO, security pack, sample benchmark plan, and a runbook for streaming fallbacks. we'll attach a checklist for migration from hosted to dedicated/private.
[08:38] Marco: can you include an example of fallback policy where 13B drops to 7B when p95 breaches? we want to see how quality and latency trade.
[08:45] Priya: yes — we'll include a sample policy and simulated result from prior customers.
[08:51] Dana: timeline recap?
[08:53] Alex: we agreed: Marco shares traces by 2028-02-07, Alex sends pricing/TCO by 2028-02-03, Priya sends streaming fallback runbook by 2028-02-08, and then we aim to have benchmark results in ~2 weeks after traces.
[09:10] Sofia: final note — we'll compile SOC2 questions and sync with Alex next week.
[09:15] Alex: great. thanks all. we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invites for the on-prem deep dive.
[09:23] [end recording]

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache"), speaker labels simplified, some timestamps approximate.
